findings.text: follow-on: the assertion is written as a substring test, `[name for name in CREW_VIEWS if name not in result["detail"]]`, and nine of the nineteen registry names also occur in the refusal's own explanatory prose that follows the composed list (reckon/mcp_views.py:3637-3642 names lanes, routing, runs, scores, velocity, fleet, plan-review and findings, and 'cross-ledger cost view' contains 'ledger'). So the assertion reddens only for a name absent from the whole detail, not for one dropped from the composed list: deleting 'runs' from line 3635 leaves 'runs is the compact joined view' standing and the test stays green. The negative control chose 'models', which the prose does not repeat, so it exercises exactly the one class the assertion does catch and none of the nine it misses. The planned regression ('a view added to CREW_VIEWS is named without a second edit') is still caught, because a newly registered name appears in no prose; the exposed gap is the drift in the other direction, a name silently dropped from the composed list.

follow-on: the head gate log's first line reads `# rev 001955d96 001955d965c1cd88cab944c0ef4ac2e083712057 tree ...`, the base commit, because the head gate ran at 01:44 with the fix still uncommitted and the commit landed at 01:49. The head result is real (1 failed, 44 passed) and the manifest's artifacts repeat it, but the log's own revision header names the base sha, so a reader comparing the log's `# rev` against `reviewed_head_sha` finds them different and cannot tell from the log alone which content was measured. The negative-control log carries the distinguisher ('(worktree files, uncommitted)') that this one omits.
